example.caption: Minimal 3-class DAL tutorial (DUNE-DAQ/dal): inheritance, enum + integer ranges, default (init) values, is-not-null, and a one-to-many relationship; the matching data file shows real objects. [Sources: https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/dal - schema/dal/tutorial.schema.xml, scripts/dal_testing.data.xml]
example.schema-file: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="ASCII"?> <!-- oks-schema version 2.2 --> <oks-schema> <info name="" type="" num-of-items="3" oks-format="schema" oks-version="862f2957270" created-by="jcfree" created-on="mu2edaq13.fnal.gov" creation-time="20230123T223700" last-modified-by="jcfree" last-modified-on="mu2edaq13.fnal.gov" last-modification-time="20230123T223700"/> <class name="Application" description="A software executable" is-abstract="yes"> <attribute name="Name" description="Name of the executable, including full path" type="string" init-value="Unknown" is-not-null="yes"/> </class> <class name="ReadoutApplication" description="An executable which reads out subdetectors"> <superclass name="Application"/> <attribute name="SubDetector" description="An enum to describe what type of subdetector it can read out" type="enum" range="PMT,WireChamber" init-value="WireChamber"/> </class> <class name="RCApplication" description="An executable which allows users to control datataking"> <superclass name="Application"/> <attribute name="Timeout" description="Seconds to wait before giving up on a transition" type="u16" range="1..3600" init-value="20" is-not-null="yes"/> <relationship name="ApplicationsControlled" description="Applications RC is in charge of" class-type="Application" low-cc="one" high-cc="many"/> </class> </oks-schema>
example.data-file: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="ASCII"?> <!-- oks-data version 2.2 --> <oks-data> <include><file path="../share/schema/dal/core.schema.xml"/></include> <obj class="Partition" id="ToyPartition"> <rel name="OnlineInfrastructure" class="OnlineSegment" id="ToyOnlineSegment"/> <rel name="DefaultHost" class="Computer" id="toyhost.fnal.gov"/> <rel name="Disabled"> <ref class="ResourceBase" id="AProblematicResource"/> </rel> </obj> <obj class="ResourceBase" id="AProblematicResource"/> <obj class="RunControlApplication" id="ToyRunControlApplication"> <attr name="InterfaceName" type="string" val="rc/commander"/> <attr name="ActionTimeout" type="s32" val="10"/> <attr name="IfExitsUnexpectedly" type="enum" val="Error"/> <attr name="IfFailsToStart" type="enum" val="Error"/> <rel name="Program" class="Binary" id="rc_controller"/> <rel name="ExplicitTag" class="Tag" id="ToyTag"/> </obj> <obj class="OnlineSegment" id="ToyOnlineSegment"> <attr name="T0_ProjectTag" type="string" val="data_test"/> <rel name="IsControlledBy" class="RunControlApplication" id="ToyRunControlApplication"/> <rel name="InitialPartition" class="Partition" id="ToyPartition"/> <rel name="Applications"> <ref class="CustomLifetimeApplication" id="SomeApp"/> </rel> <rel name="Segments"> <ref class="Segment" id="ToyChildSegment"/> </rel> </obj> <obj class="Computer" id="toyhost.fnal.gov"> <attr name="HW_Tag" type="enum" val="x86_64-centos7"/> <attr name="SW_Tag" type="enum" val="gcc49-opt"/> <attr name="NumberOfCores" type="s16" val="2"/> <attr name="RLogin" type="string" val="ssh"/> </obj> </oks-data>

example.caption: The ATLAS/TDAQ core schema (real production classes). The run-level entry point is the Partition: it holds top-level Segments, the online infrastructure, disabled components, tags, parameters and (important) the database attributes DBPath/DBName/DBVersion — DBVersion is the OKS git SHA used for the partition, i.e. the answer to "what configuration was used". Methods get_config_version()/set_config_version() are the DAL interface for that. Also shows the C++/Java dual-language method bodies typical of dal-generated code. [Source: https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/dal - schema/dal/core.schema.xml]
example.schema-file: <class name="Partition" description="The class describes TDAQ configuration including top-level segments, disabled components, various TDAQ base and user specific parameters."> <attribute name="RepositoryRoot" description="Temporary sw installation area having highest priority" type="string"/> <attribute name="IPCRef" description="IPC init reference; default from TDAQ_IPC_INIT_REF env" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_IPC_INIT_REF)"/> <attribute name="DBPath" description="Locations of database repositories (OKS_DB_ROOT); default from TDAQ_DB_PATH" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_PATH)"/> <attribute name="DBName" description="Name of the OKS data file; default from TDAQ_DB_DATA" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_DATA)"/> <attribute name="DBVersion" description="Database version (SHA key) if GIT repository is used; default from TDAQ_DB_VERSION" type="string" init-value="$(TDAQ_DB_VERSION)"/> <attribute name="DBTechnology" description="Config database technology implementation" type="enum" range="rdbconfig,oksconflibs" init-value="rdbconfig"/> <attribute name="RunTypes" type="string" is-multi-value="yes"/> <relationship name="Segments" description="Top-level segments composing given partition. To disable a segment, add it to Disabled instead of removing it." class-type="Segment" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="yes"/> <relationship name="OnlineInfrastructure" description="Defines online infrastructure segment." class-type="OnlineSegment" low-cc="one" high-cc="one" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="Disabled" description="Lists segments and resources which are temporary disabled." class-type="Component" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no" ordered="yes"/> <relationship name="DefaultHost" description="Host to run all applications with empty 'RunsOn'." class-type="Computer" low-cc="zero" high-cc="one" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="DefaultTags" description="Default tags used to select binaries for applications without explicit tag." class-type="Tag" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no"/> <relationship name="ProcessEnvironment" description="Process environment for any application ran in given partition." class-type="Parameter" low-cc="zero" high-cc="many" is-composite="no"/> <method name="set_config_version" description="Set configuration version, i.e. OKS GIT repository SHA. The partition infrastructure has to be running."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="void set_config_version(const std::string& name, bool reload) const"/> <method-implementation language="java" prototype="void set_config_version(final String version, boolean reload) throws config.GenericException, config.SystemException, config.NotFoundException, config.NotValidException"/> </method> <method name="get_config_version" description="Return configuration version used by given partition, i.e. OKS GIT repository SHA. The partition infrastructure has to be running."> <method-implementation language="c++" prototype="std::string get_config_version() const"/> <method-implementation language="java" prototype="String get_config_version() throws config.GenericException, config.SystemException, config.NotFoundException, config.NotValidException"/> </method> </class>

example.caption: The OKS data type reference (CERN oks repo test): all attribute types (bool..u64, float, double, date, time, string, enum, class), multi-value attributes, hex format, and the compact "data" format (attr val inside tag). Good grounding for translating attribute names to type-correct query values. [Sources: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks - test/all_types.schema.xml, test/test.data.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="Element" description="It is a class to describe a person"> <attribute name="Boolean" type="bool"/> <attribute name="IntS8" type="s8"/> <attribute name="IntU8" type="u8"/> <attribute name="IntS16" type="s16"/> <attribute name="IntU16" type="u16"/> <attribute name="IntS32" type="s32"/> <attribute name="IntU32" type="u32"/> <attribute name="IntS64" type="s64"/> <attribute name="Int64" type="u64"/> <attribute name="Float" type="float"/> <attribute name="Double" type="double"/> <attribute name="String" type="string"/> <attribute name="Date" type="date"/> <attribute name="Time" type="time"/> <attribute name="Enum" type="enum" range="one,two,three,four,five" init-value="one"/> <attribute name="Class" type="class" init-value="Container"/> <attribute name="ArrayIntS8" type="s8" is-multi-value="yes"/> <attribute name="ArrayString" type="string" is-multi-value="yes"/> <attribute name="ArrayEnum" type="enum" range="one,two,three,four,five" is-multi-value="yes" init-value="one"/> <attribute name="HexIntU8" type="u8" format="hex"/> <attribute name="HexIntU64" type="u64" format="hex"/> </class> </oks-schema>
example.data-file: <oks-data> <include><file path="all_types.schema.xml"/></include> <obj class="Element" id="o1-good"> <attr name="Boolean" type="bool" val="1"/> <attr name="IntS8" type="s8" val="-128"/> <attr name="IntU16" type="u16" val="50000"/> <attr name="IntS64" type="s64" val="-10000000000"/> <attr name="Float" type="float" val="3.1415"/> <attr name="Double" type="double" val="2.1928"/> <attr name="String" type="string" val="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."/> <attr name="Date" type="date" val="20240809"/> <attr name="Time" type="time" val="20240809T150647"/> <attr name="Enum" type="enum" val="one"/> <attr name="Class" type="class" val="Container"/> <attr name="ArrayIntS8" type="s8"> <data val="1"/> <data val="-1"/> <data val="127"/> </attr> <attr name="HexIntU8" type="u8" val="0xff"/> <attr name="HexIntU64" type="u64" val="0x123456789abcdef"/> </obj> <obj class="Container" id="o1-good-container"> <attr name="Date" type="date" val="20240829"/> <attr name="Time" type="time" val="20240829T104831"/> <attr name="Enum" type="enum" val="one"/> <attr name="Class" type="class" val="Container"/> <rel name="Root" class="Element" id="o1-good"/> <rel name="Contains"> <ref class="Element" id="o1-good"/> </rel> </obj> </oks-data>

example.caption: Classic DAQ configuration classes (oks_utils tests): software objects, computers, programs, environment variables and the (dynamic) Process class. Shows the old naming conventions still used in production DBs. [Source: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks_utils - tests/DAQ-Configuration.schema.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="Computer" description="Describes an abstract computer."> <attribute name="Name" description="Computer name (e.g. pc-tdaq-onl-01)" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="OSType" description="Operating system type" type="enum" range="Linux,SunOS,Win32"/> <attribute name="CPUSpeed" description="CPU speed in MHz" type="u16"/> </class> <class name="Environment" description="The Environment class is used to describe environment variables and their values. These variables are defined and values are assigned before starting the corresponding process."> <attribute name="Name" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="Value" type="string"/> </class> <class name="Program" description="This class is used to describe platform dependent part of DAQ software component. It defines default parameters to start a program (command line, environment, priority, etc.)."> <attribute name="CommandLine" type="string"/> <attribute name="Priority" type="s32" init-value="0"/> </class> <class name="Process" description="The Process class is used to describe a dynamic physical part of a software object: logical name of the process, process id, date and time of start, real process priority and privileges."> <attribute name="Id" type="string" is-not-null="yes"/> <attribute name="StartTime" type="time"/> <relationship name="Program" class-type="Program" low-cc="one" high-cc="one"/> <relationship name="RunsOn" class-type="Computer" low-cc="one" high-cc="one"/> </class> </oks-schema>

example.caption: The oks2coral archiving schema: ConfigVersions records which archive (schema/data version) of the OKS database was used for a given run — the offline counterpart of the online "r380689@all_hosts" git tags. [Source: https://gitlab.cern.ch/atlas-tdaq-software/oks2coral - data/oks-archive-info.xml]
example.schema-file: <oks-schema> <class name="ConfigVersions" description="The class is used to store archive versions of the OKS database used for given run."> <superclass name="Info"/> <attribute name="Run" type="u32" is-not-null="yes" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="SchemaVersion" type="u32" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="DataVersion" type="u32" init-value="0"/> <attribute name="TotalVersion" type="string"/> <attribute name="Time" type="time" init-value="11-10"/> </class> </oks-schema>
